Now we will load the dataset 

```{r datasets}
library(readr)
steam <- read_csv("Downloads/Blinded_data_sets/dataset30_ 9779 .csv")

## Ctree synthesis
set.seed(123)
ctree_data <- syn(
  steam,
  method = "ctree",
  m = 1
)$syn

head(ctree_data)
```

## Now let us check the causal utility for CART

```{r causal utlity}
## Regression Adjustment

real_reg <- glm(
  Y ~ W + x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 + x6,
  family = binomial,
  data = steam
)

ctree_reg <- glm(
  Y ~ W + x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 + x6,
  family = binomial,
  data = ctree_data
)

## Here we have done regression adjustmnent for the real and cart synthetic dataset

real_OR <- exp(coef(real_reg)["W"])

ctree_OR <- exp(coef(ctree_reg)["W"])

comparison_OR <- data.frame(

  Dataset = c("Original","Ctree"),

  Odds_Ratio = c(real_OR, ctree_OR)

)

comparison_OR

## Both have a different odds ratio

## Original	 7.381430			
## CART	     5.635388


real_CI <- exp(confint.default(real_reg)["W",])

ctree_CI <- exp(confint.default(ctree_reg)["W",])

CI_table <- data.frame(

  Dataset = c("Original","Ctree"),

  OR = c(real_OR, cart_OR),

  Lower = c(real_CI[1], cart_CI[1]),

  Upper = c(real_CI[2], cart_CI[2])

)

CI_table

## Original	7.381430	2.609966	20.87595	
## Ctree	5.635388	1.676858	18.93875	
```
## G computation

```{r g formula}
## G-computation

estimate_ATE <- function(data){

  model <- glm(

    Y ~ W + x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 + x6,

    family = binomial,

    data = data

  )

  treated <- data
  treated$W <- 1

  untreated <- data
  untreated$W <- 0

  risk1 <- predict(
    model,
    newdata = treated,
    type = "response"
  )

  risk0 <- predict(
    model,
    newdata = untreated,
    type = "response"
  )

  mean(risk1 - risk0)

}

## ATE results 

ATE_real <- estimate_ATE(steam)

ATE_ctree <- estimate_ATE(ctree_data)

ATE_results <- data.frame(

  Dataset = c("Original","Ctree"),

  ATE = c(ATE_real, ATE_ctree)

)

ATE_results

## Compare the absolute erros

ATE_results$Absolute_Error <- c(

  0,

  abs(ATE_real - ATE_ctree)

)

ATE_results

## Here the absolute error is slightly small comapred to the previous CART(0.79)
```
## IPTW

```{r iptw}
## IPTW

estimate_IPTW <- function(data){

  ps_model <- glm(

    W ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 + x6,

    family = binomial,

    data = data

  )

  ps <- predict(
    ps_model,
    type = "response"
  )

  weights <- ifelse(

    data$W == 1,

    1 / ps,

    1 / (1 - ps)

  )

  outcome_model <- glm(

    Y ~ W,

    family = binomial,

    weights = weights,

    data = data

  )

  exp(coef(outcome_model)["W"])

}

## Comapte the IPTW weights

iptw_real <- estimate_IPTW(steam)

iptw_ctree <- estimate_IPTW(ctree_data)

IPTW_table <- data.frame(

  Dataset = c("Original","Ctree"),

  IPTW_OR = c(iptw_real, iptw_ctree)

)

IPTW_table
```
## PS score distirbutions

```{r PS}
real_ps_model <- glm(

  W ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 + x6,

  family = binomial,

  data = steam

)

steam$PS <- predict(
  real_ps_model,
  type = "response"
)

ctree_ps_model <- glm(

  W ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 + x6,

  family = binomial,

  data = ctree_data

)

ctree_data$PS <- predict(
  ctree_ps_model,
  type = "response"
)

## Plot


ggplot() +

  geom_density(

    data = steam,

    aes(PS, colour = "Original"),

    linewidth = 1

  ) +

  geom_density(

    data = ctree_data,

    aes(PS, colour = "Ctree"),

    linewidth = 1

  ) +

  labs(

    title = "Propensity Score Distribution",

    x = "Propensity Score",

    colour = ""

  )
```

```{r final}
causal_results <- data.frame(

  Dataset = c("Original","Ctree"),

  Regression_OR = c(real_OR, ctree_OR),

  IPTW_OR = c(iptw_real, iptw_ctree),

  Gcomp_ATE = c(ATE_real, ATE_ctree)

)

causal_results
```
## Causal error framework

```{r causal error}
causal_error <- data.frame(

  Measure = c(
    "Regression OR",
    "IPTW OR",
    "G-computation ATE"
  ),

  Original = c(
    7.381430,
    4.994238,
    0.2678132
  ),

  Ctree = c(
    5.930619,
    5.01206,
    0.2743175
  )

)

causal_error$Absolute_Error <-
  abs(causal_error$Original - causal_error$Ctree)

causal_error$Relative_Error <-
  100 * causal_error$Absolute_Error /
  causal_error$Original

causal_error
```
The synthetic data does not reverse the direction of the causal effect.
